name: Tsukaito Wrap Cord — Silence
description:
The binding cord wrapped around the tsuka (handle) of Silence in the traditional tsukaito pattern — a diagonal crosshatch that provides grip texture and secures the underlying handle structure. On Silence, the tsukaito wraps the graphene ultracapacitor module housing rather than a traditional wooden core, and carries a secondary function: the cord is woven loosely enough that the electroluminescence of the charged bank is faintly visible through the weave in low light.

The cord is a high-tenacity polymer braid — not silk or cotton as in traditional construction, but a material that resists sweat, blood, and repeated high-grip use without stretching or fraying. It is midnight black with no contrast marking. Traditional tsukaito uses decorative diamonds formed by the crossing pattern; on Silence the pattern is functional and tight, prioritizing grip surface area over aesthetics.

Kyle rewraps the tsukaito approximately once per year or when the cord shows fraying at high-contact points. He does this himself. It takes about forty minutes and a specific tension he has had to learn through failure — too tight and the wrap damps the luminescence below useful visibility; too loose and it slips under hard grip pressure.
specifications:
Material: high-tenacity polymer braid
Color: midnight black
Length per application: approximately 6 meters (standard katana tsuka)
Pattern: traditional tsukaito diamond crosshatch
Function: grip surface + luminescence diffuser for supercapacitor charge indicator

cost.installation_labor: Self-applied. First application without prior experience: 2–3 hours. Kyle applies in approximately 40 minutes.
cost.availability: Traditional swordsmithing supply channels. Available from specialist suppliers in GLMZ's artisan districts without licensing requirements.
cost.notes: Consumable. Replace annually under heavy use or when grip texture becomes visibly worn. Improper tension affects luminescence readability.
